newsitem.title: FRANCE: French truckers threaten to block Spanish border.
newsitem.headline: French truckers threaten to block Spanish border.

text.p: Two French truckers' unions urged drivers to mount a blockade along France's border with Spain from Sunday evening to persuade the European Union to regulate working conditions.

"While there are European regulations for all other professions, transport industry bosses have not wanted them," said Roger Poletti, secretary general of the trucking section of the Socialist-dominated Force Ouvriere union.
"As far as Brussels is concerned, what we want goes against the grain of the laissez-faire environment sought by the haulage employers," he told France Info radio.
Topping the truckers' demands were better working conditions.

The truckers have accused employers of failing to honour a pact last year granting retirement at 55 instead of 60 for drivers with 25 years' service, as well as providing for sick pay, travel expenses, union rights and a ban on Sunday driving.

Last month truckers barricaded fuel depots in some parts of France in protest at the employers' policies, but the protest was dropped after a union member was crushed to death by a lorry he was trying to stop.

The appeal for a new blockade was issued two days after hundreds of Spanish truck drivers and farmers blockaded the French border in an unrelated protest against violent attacks by French drivers and farmers on the Spanish trucks and produce.
The Spanish protesters blocked the major crossing at La Jonquera.
French truckers and farmers have been blocking Spanish vehicles and burning or dumping the fruit and vegetables they were carrying in protest at low Spanish produce prices.
The French farmers want tighter controls on cheaper imports of vegetables and fruit.
